claim: Flutter currently declares Android, iOS, Windows and web deployment support; support does not establish VIDA feature parity.
Flutter's current recommended native C interop path is package_ffi with build hooks; native dart:ffi does not provide web interop.
flutter_rust_bridge registry showed stable 2.13.0 and prerelease 2.14.0-beta.2 on 2026-09-19.
flutter_rust_bridge offers generated Flutter/Dart to Rust binding, including async methods and streams; it does not itself define VIDA durable event semantics.
flutter_rust_bridge cancellation guidance uses application-level or Tokio cancellation tokens rather than an automatic durable-operation cancellation guarantee.
Flutter web lacks Dart isolates in the documented model; a background isolate cannot receive unsolicited host-platform messages.
Android can restrict background jobs, alarms and networking for restricted applications; OS scheduling must be tested rather than inferred from Flutter or Rust.
Apple treats background notifications as low priority, without delivery guarantee, and may throttle them.
Flutter provides accessibility support but recommends real TalkBack and VoiceOver checks before release.
Tauri's Windows shell uses an OS WebView with a Rust host, implying a WebView-to-Rust boundary distinct from Dart FFI.
Tauri supports Rust commands with arguments, results, typed-serializable errors, async behavior, channels and binary response paths.
Tauri Windows uses WebView2, whose installer/runtime availability must be part of release qualification.
Tauri offers MSI/NSIS Windows installers and online, offline and fixed WebView2 deployment modes; offline distribution increases installer size.
WebView2 uses browser, renderer and helper processes, so Tauri Windows memory measurement must include the process group.
Tauri capabilities constrain frontend access but cannot protect against malicious/insecure Rust code, lax scopes or incorrect command checks.
Tauri updater automatically quits the Windows application before installing an update; a pre-exit hook exists.
UniFFI officially supports Kotlin, Swift and Python bindings and does not package a Rust library for target platforms.
UniFFI does not directly support future cancellation; its guidance calls for a library-specific cancellation channel.
UniFFI does not ship a first-party WASM/browser binding generator; external generators can target its configured WASM scaffolding.
For wasm32-unknown-unknown, normal Rust std::fs and std::net are not available as native facilities and return errors.
A current first-party Iroh browser/Wasm example is relay-only because browsers cannot open raw UDP/QUIC sockets; this does not disprove all future alternative transports.
Flutter and Dart do not provide ABI compatibility across compiler releases; matching SDK/build artifacts matter.
The approved VIDA composition model makes Messenger, Knowledge and Projects schema-driven AppInstances in a Space and keeps Space security/sync separate from mandatory top-level navigation.
Approved VIDA NFRs require crash recovery, exactly-once domain apply under duplicate delivery, platform-specific conformance and defer quantitative SLOs.
Approved VidaNodeHost contract requires cancellable typed operations and start/suspend/resume/shutdown lifecycle but defers concrete Rust/FFI and background implementation.
Dioxus was expressly retracted as an inherited VIDA UI decision; Flutter in an older visual prototype and .NET/Blazor in older architecture text are not approved shell selections.
A VIDA app package is described as portable across storage providers; separate DataSchema/FormSchema/PageLayout/ViewDefinition and presentation variants remain proposal detail.
The raw corpus proposes a package lifecycle with install consent, capabilities, version pin, migrations, assets and trust tiers; exact v1 extent is open.
A status-tagged VIDA working note enumerates calculated UI capability states and requires trusted command recheck.
The user asked for compact account switching and persistent app/navigation access; exact rail geometry and per-app stack behavior were assistant proposals.
The user described centralized SaaS/GEO city and business contexts; same business ID across entry points, public website and placement moderation are derived design proposals.
An older validation proposal requires same authoritative command outcome across site, bot and client and says City Portal SaaS tests do not prove offline/P2P/mobile behavior.
Large-conversation selective subscriptions, bounded queues and resync_required are proposed; 50k clients and latency numbers are scenarios/targets, not measured VIDA capacity.
The corpus proposes durable reminders/missed-job handling after process shutdown; executor authority and platform scheduling remain open.
Full/Mobile/Browser node profiles and constrained ESP32/e-ink UI are proposals; edge is not a v1 platform gate.
The corpus discusses browser local Wasm/OPFS/relay and gateway alternatives without accepting a browser capability profile.
Exact schema availability is identified as an offline-decode risk; projection rebuild and index-progress behavior are proposed recovery cases.
Desktop local gRPC/UDS/Named-Pipe sidecar and mobile FFI are older .NET-shell proposals, not an accepted Tauri/Rust process topology.
After the user rejected email, the earlier Chatmail/Delta Chat core recommendation was retracted; JSON-RPC remained only possible reference.
The working architecture accepts provider-neutral package/resource semantics and cross-provider identity tests; CBOR/PDM specifics in a separate note remain recommendation, not final wire contract.
Flutter platform-specific plugin code must be built into the application; ordinary Flutter packages are not arbitrary installable runtime plugins.

Flutter deferred Android/web components require predeclared deferred imports; Android new code requires rebuilding and uploading the whole AAB, so this is not arbitrary post-release code installation.
